key_insight: A physics-informed neural network with exact boundary and initial constraints accurately recovers the shear piezoelectric coefficient e₁₅ from sparse, noisy simulated wavefields.
engineering_relevance: The approach could enable nondestructive characterization of shear-mode coupling in PMUTs and surface acoustic wave devices without dedicated resonance-test specimens.
method: Embed spatial distance functions and temporal multipliers into network outputs to enforce boundary and initial conditions exactly.
Train on coupled electro-elastodynamic equations and sparse observations, eliminating boundary and initial-condition penalty weights.
Nondimensionalize governing coefficients to comparable scales for optimization.
evidence_signal: On finite-element data sampled along one subsurface line, mean e₁₅ error was 1.19% at 30 dB noise and 0.65–2.71% across a 40–0 dB noise sweep.
watch_item: Validation is limited to simulated plane-strain PZT-5H data; performance on physical measurements and more complex geometries remains untested.
paper_title: Identifying the Shear Piezoelectric Coefficient using Physics-Informed Neural Networks under Exact Boundary and Initial Constraints
